title: Governance Concepts: Laws, Frameworks, Policies, Standards and Procedures

header.html: 1.3 Understand governance concepts: Regulations and laws; Frameworks and guidelines; Policies, standards (for example ISO, Center for Internet Security), procedures
the official ISC2 CC exam outline

html:
1Governance in one sentence

Governance is how the leaders of an organization direct and oversee security so that it supports the business and meets its duties. Management then carries out that direction.

Level Role Example
Governance Sets direction and checks results The board approves the security strategy and policy
Management Plans and runs the work The security manager runs the program
Operations Does the daily tasks An analyst applies a procedure
Exam tip

. Governance = direction and oversight. Management = execution. Senior management owns policy and accepts risk.

2Regulations and laws

Laws and regulations are mandatory and come from governments or regulators. Breaking them can bring fines, lawsuits or prison and harms reputation. Compliance means following them.

Rule Area
GDPR (EU) Privacy of personal data of people in the EU
HIPAA (US) Health information
SOX (US) Financial reporting accuracy of public companies
GLBA (US) Financial institutions and customer data
FERPA (US) Student education records
CCPA (California) Consumer privacy

PCI DSS (payment card security) is not a law: it is an industry standard that card brands require by contract.

Exam tip

. A law is mandatory by government. A standard like PCI DSS is mandatory by contract. When laws from several places apply, the strictest applicable one often drives the design.

3Frameworks and guidelines

A framework is a structured set of good practices to organize a security program. It is voluntary unless a law or contract requires it.

Framework What it gives you
NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) Functions Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover
NIST SP 800-53 A catalog of security and privacy controls
ISO/IEC 27001 Requirements for an information security management system (ISMS); organizations can be audited against it
ISO/IEC 27002 Guidance on the controls
CIS Controls A prioritized list of practical safeguards from the Center for Internet Security
COBIT A framework for IT governance and management

4Policies, standards, procedures and guidelines

Document Purpose Mandatory? Example
Policy High-level rule that states what and why; approved by senior management Yes "All laptops must be encrypted"
Standard Specific requirements that support a policy Yes "Use AES with a 256-bit key"
Procedure Step-by-step instructions for a task Yes "How to enable disk encryption"
Guideline Recommendations and advice No "Prefer a passphrase of several words"

A baseline is the minimum secure configuration for a type of system. Common policies: acceptable use, password, remote access, data classification, data retention, incident response, bring your own device (BYOD).

Exam tip

. Policy says what and why. Standard says which. Procedure says how. Guideline is only advice. The order: policy first, then standards, then procedures.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Which document gives step-by-step instructions for restoring a database from backup?

  • AA policy, which states the high-level rule
  • BA procedure, which lists the steps to follow
  • CA standard, which sets the specific requirement
  • DA guideline, which offers optional advice
Show the answer

Answer: B. A procedure is a set of step-by-step instructions for a task.

S2A document says that passwords must have at least 14 characters. Which type of document is it?

  • AA standard, which states a specific requirement
  • BA guideline, which is only a recommendation for staff
  • CA policy, which states the high-level purpose
  • DA procedure, which describes each step
Show the answer

Answer: A. A specific, mandatory requirement that supports a policy is a standard.

S3A company stores payment card data and must follow PCI DSS. How is PCI DSS best described?

  • AAn industry standard required by contract
  • BA government law with criminal penalties
  • CAn optional guideline for large companies
  • DA framework used only for privacy audits
Show the answer

Answer: A. PCI DSS is an industry standard that card brands require by contract; it is not a law.

S4A team wants to build a security program using the functions Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover, plus Govern. Which framework is this?

  • ACOBIT for IT governance and management
  • BISO/IEC 27001 for an ISMS
  • CThe NIST Cybersecurity Framework
  • DThe CIS Controls with prioritized safeguards
Show the answer

Answer: C. The NIST Cybersecurity Framework is organized around those functions, including Govern.

S5Who is responsible for approving the security policy of an organization?

  • ASenior management or the board
  • BThe newest security analyst
  • CThe external penetration tester
  • DThe help desk team lead
Show the answer

Answer: A. Policy is approved by senior management, which sets direction and owns the risk.

S6A recommendation that staff should use a long passphrase, but it is not required, is an example of what?

  • AA policy, which is mandatory
  • BA standard, which is mandatory
  • CA regulation, which is a law
  • DA guideline, which is optional
Show the answer

Answer: D. A guideline is a recommendation and is not mandatory.

5.2 Recall questions

R1Which document is mandatory and high level?

Show the answer

A policy.

R2Which document is optional advice?

Show the answer

A guideline.

R3What does ISO/IEC 27001 define?

Show the answer

Requirements for an information security management system.

R4Is PCI DSS a law?

Show the answer

No, it is an industry standard required by contract.

R5What are the NIST CSF functions?

Show the answer

Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover.

R6Who approves policy?

Show the answer

Senior management.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Governance leaders direct and oversee; management executes
Laws mandatory by government: GDPR, HIPAA, SOX
PCI DSS industry standard, mandatory by contract
Frameworks NIST CSF, NIST 800-53, ISO 27001 and 27002, CIS Controls, COBIT
Documents policy (what, why), standard (which), procedure (how), guideline (advice)
